events.action: Displays opening titles and credits
events.description: The film opens with the MGM lion trademark, title cards, and cast and crew credits accompanied by orchestral music.

events.action: Enters a dimly lit room
events.description: Edward Wales enters a dark room near shuttered doors and inspects the room and floor with a flashlight.

events.action: Converse inside the crime room
events.description: Wales offers money to servant Ram Das to leave him alone in the room for ten minutes, but Ram Das refuses due to police orders.

events.action: Secretly watches Wales and Ram Das
events.description: Professor Feringeea peeks from behind a carved wooden screen while Wales attempts to bribe Ram Das.
events.uncertainty: Actor identity inferred from cast list

events.action: Argue as Wales increases the bribe offer
events.description: Wales offers up to thirty rupees to Ram Das, who speaks in Hindi to another servant and insists on locking the doors until police arrive.

events.action: Communicate via telephone
events.description: Ram Das places a call to Commissioner Grimshaw to report Wales' unauthorized presence in Spencer Lee's room.

events.action: Argue over the telephone regarding the murder suspect
events.description: Wales claims he can identify the woman who killed Spencer Lee but refuses to state her name on the phone, claiming she is prominent in official circles.

events.action: Discuss Wales' statement and police records
events.description: Grimshaw tells Delzante that Wales claims a veiled woman committed the murder, while Delzante notes official records confirm Lee's last visitor was heavily veiled.

events.action: Review the details of the crime scene discovery
events.description: Grimshaw recounts that Lee was found stabbed in the back and died in Wales' arms, noting that no fingerprints were found on the untouched tea cup.

events.actor: Commissioner Grimshaw and Sir Roscoe Crosby
events.action: Speak on the telephone
events.description: Grimshaw calls Sir Roscoe Crosby to inform him that Inspector Delzante has arrived in Calcutta, and Sir Roscoe offers the residency's full assistance.

events.actor: Sir Roscoe Crosby, Lady Crosby, and Helen
events.action: Discuss the investigation while playing cards
events.description: Sir Roscoe informs Lady Crosby and Helen of Delzante's arrival, prompting Lady Crosby to express apprehension about the identity of the veiled woman.

events.action: Converse on the terrace about marriage
events.description: Richard asks Nelly to marry him, but Nelly hesitates due to their social class difference and her position as his mother's secretary.

events.action: Embrace and agree to inform his family
events.description: Richard reassures Nelly that class differences do not matter to him and convinces her to bring the topic to his family immediately.

events.actor: Richard Crosby, Nelly O'Neill, Sir Roscoe, Lady Crosby, and Helen
events.action: Announce their marriage plans to the family
events.description: Richard brings Nelly inside to meet his family, who react warmly and express complete approval of Richard's choice.

events.action: Share a supportive conversation
events.description: Lady Crosby recounts her own background as a schoolteacher when marrying Richard's father, offering words of encouragement to Nelly.

events.action: Performs a trick holding a vertical rope
events.description: Professor Feringeea stands on the terrace holding an upright suspended length of rope.

events.actor: Man in turban and man in tuxedo
events.action: Demonstrating strangulation with a cord
events.description: A man wearing a turban demonstrates a strangulation technique using a cord around the neck of a man in a tuxedo. The victim playfully chokes while other guests react in amusement.

events.actor: Man in turban and man in tuxedo
events.action: Discussing the murder of Spencer Lee
events.description: The man in the turban claims that Thugs never spill blood, asserting that this proves they were not involved in Spencer Lee's murder. The other man asks whether Lee's published articles attacking the cult led to his death.

events.actor: Party guests in the living room
events.action: Proposing to hold a séance
events.description: Guests gather around drinks and propose holding a séance later that evening with a visiting fortune teller. They debate whether spiritualism and mediumship should be taken seriously.

events.action: Proposing to ask Spencer Lee's spirit who killed him
events.description: Howard suggests asking the spirit of Spencer Lee during the séance to name his murderer. Female guests protest that asking such a direct question would be sacrilegious.

events.action: Confronting each other over the engagement announcement
events.description: Richard Crosby demands an apology from Edward Wales regarding remarks about his fiancée. Wales asks Sir Roscoe Crosby to withhold announcing Richard's engagement to Miss O'Neill that evening.

events.action: Defending her mother against implied criticism
events.description: Helen O'Neill steps forward to defend her mother from any negative allegations. Wales clarifies that he does not know her mother and has never heard of her.

events.actor: Sir Roscoe Crosby, Richard Crosby, and Edward Wales
events.action: Agreeing to delay the engagement announcement for twenty-four hours
events.description: Sir Roscoe Crosby agrees to delay announcing the engagement for twenty-four hours on Wales's recommendation. Sir Roscoe cautions that he expects a complete and satisfactory explanation the next day.

events.action: Announcing the arrival of Madame Rosalie La Grange
events.description: Lady Crosby informs the room that the fortune teller Madame La Grange has arrived. Some guests mockingly anticipate poking fun at her during the session.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange and Edward Wales
events.action: Entering the room and greeting the hostess
events.description: Madame La Grange enters wearing dark clothing and a head wrap, greeting Lady Crosby and guests in an Irish accent. Edward Wales introduces her to the room.

events.action: Explaining how she deduced the unpaid bazaar bill
events.description: Madame La Grange reveals she read an unpaid bazaar bill found in a guest's handbag left in the hallway and matched the handbag fabric to the guest's dress. She openly admits to this trickery to prove how easily people are duped.

events.action: Demonstrating how she produces spirit tapping sounds
events.description: Madame La Grange produces loud knocking sounds by clicking her big toe against a wooden device inside her shoe. She demonstrates this trick to show how fake mediums fake spirit rappings.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange and Edward Wales
events.action: Promising an honest séance without fake tricks
events.description: Madame La Grange promises that although her profession usually involves trickery, tonight she will perform an honest séance. Wales confirms no money will be exchanged for her services under these test conditions.

events.action: Discussing table levitation and spirit phenomena
events.description: Guests discuss previous experiences with table turning and spiritual manifestations. Wales reassures them about the conditions for tonight's séance.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange and host
events.action: Asking for a small card table to perform the séance
events.description: Madame La Grange asks the host to bring a small card table for the séance. Guests prepare to take their seats around the table.

events.action: Demonstrates table levitation trickery to the guests.
events.description: Madame La Grange places her hands on a small folding table and tilts it to demonstrate trickery used by fraudulent mediums. The surrounding guests watch her physical demonstration with amusement and curiosity.

events.action: Slams the table down and offers to conduct a trance seance.
events.description: Madame La Grange sets the table down and acknowledges to the company that she cannot fool them with trickery. She offers to enter a trance state and contact her spirit control named Laughing Eyes.

events.action: Feigns receiving a spirit message before claiming skepticism interrupted it.
events.description: Madame La Grange pauses dramatizing a trance and claims her spirit control has fled due to the presence of unbelievers in the room. She asserts that she might as well leave and attend to her business.

events.action: Helen begs Madame La Grange to stay for the seance.
events.description: Helen approaches Madame La Grange and earnestly pleads with her to stay as a personal favor. Moved by Helen's request, Madame La Grange agrees to stay and proceed with the seance.

events.actor: Edward Wales and Madame La Grange
events.action: Edward Wales sets controlled conditions for the seance.
events.description: Edward Wales warns Madame La Grange that he will closely scrutinize her manifestations. He suggests locking all doors and windows to ensure no outside accomplice can assist her.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and female guests
events.action: Madame La Grange agrees to be physically searched by the women.
events.description: Madame La Grange consents to let the ladies search her clothes and body in a private room to prove she has no hidden devices. She makes lighthearted jokes about her plain underwear as the women escort her out.

events.action: Edward Wales discloses his motive to contact the spirit of Spencer Lee.
events.description: While the women are searching the medium, Edward Wales reveals to Sir Rosco and the men that his true purpose is to find out who killed Spencer Lee. Sir Rosco and the other men discuss Spencer Lee's questionable character.

events.action: Madame La Grange is searched by the women in an adjoining room.
events.description: In a side room, the female guests check Madame La Grange's garments to ensure nothing is concealed. Helen assists her as the other women complete their search and prepare to head back.

events.action: Madame La Grange privately reveals to Helen that she is her mother.
events.description: When left alone together, Madame La Grange embraces Helen tearfully and addresses her as her daughter, expressing anxiety about embarrassing Helen in front of wealthy friends. Helen embraces her warmly and insists she feels no shame.

events.action: Edward Wales orders the room locked from the outside.
events.description: Edward Wales gives keys to the servant Chotti, instructing him to lock the room door from the hallway and remain standing guard outside until instructed otherwise.

events.action: The guests arrange chairs and take seats in a circle.
events.description: The group places thirteen chairs in a circle and takes their seats for the seance. A guest remarks nervously on the number thirteen before Madame La Grange instructs everyone to join hands.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and Edward Wales
events.action: Madame La Grange instructs participants to hold hands as lights are prepped to turn off.
events.description: Madame La Grange advises the circle that she may groan or make noise while going into trance and asks everyone to maintain hand contact. Edward Wales tells Richard to turn off the lights when ordered.

events.action: The room is darkened and a female guest screams in horror.
events.description: The lights are switched off, leaving the room in darkness while participants hold hands. A female guest suddenly screams loudly that a hand touched her face.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and female guest
events.action: The lights turn on and Madame La Grange explains the ghost hand was a test trick.
events.description: When the lights are restored, Madame La Grange calmly explains that she touched the woman's face herself to demonstrate how easily trickery occurs before having her hands bound. The startled guest expresses surprise at the illusion.

events.action: Explaining medium trickery
events.description: Madame La Grange demonstrates to the seated guests how a medium can secretly free a hand during a séance held in the dark.

events.action: Collecting handkerchiefs to bind the medium
events.description: Sir Rosco collects handkerchiefs from the gentlemen present to bind Madame La Grange securely to her chair.

events.action: Tying Madame La Grange to the chair
events.description: The gentlemen tie Madame La Grange's wrists and ankles with handkerchiefs and verify that the knots are firm.

events.action: Joining hands and turning off the lights
events.description: The guests join hands in a circle around the bound medium, and the room lights are turned off.

events.action: Entering a trance state in the dark
events.description: In total darkness, Madame La Grange hums and moans as she slips into a trance.
events.uncertainty: Visuals are pitch black during the blackout.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and Edward Wales
events.action: Channeling spirit messages
events.description: Madame La Grange speaks in a altered spirit voice regarding Spencer, letters, and a pool, while Edward Wales asks the spirit questions.
events.uncertainty: Visuals remain pitch black during the blackout.

events.action: Demanding the killer's name amid a sudden assault
events.description: Wales repeatedly demands to know who killed Spencer, which is immediately followed by sounds of a struggle, gasps, and screams in the dark.
events.uncertainty: The attack occurs in complete darkness; exact physical movements cannot be seen.

events.action: Investigating crime scene conditions
events.description: Inspector Delzante questions Sir Rosco about the locked doors, key custody, and moving the victim's body.

events.action: Addressing the missing knife and suspect pool
events.description: Inspector Delzante notes that the knife has not been located and declares every person in the room a suspect.

events.action: Stopping body removal to note guest hesitation
events.description: Delzante stops the men from carrying Wales out, pointing out that four gentlemen hesitated when asked to lift the body.

events.action: Ordering seating reconstruction
events.description: Inspector Delzante commands all participants to sit back down in the circle in their original séance seating positions.

events.action: Reconstructing guest seating positions
events.description: Madame La Grange assists Inspector Delzante by specifying where individual guests were seated prior to the blackout.

events.action: Adjusting chairs for precision
events.description: The guests swap chairs and adjust positions to ensure the reconstructed circle matches the original séance arrangement.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Sir Roscoe Crosby
events.action: Discussing Wales's seance questions prior to his murder
events.description: Inspector Delzante questions Sir Roscoe about whether the seance messages were intended solely for Wales. Sir Roscoe confirms Wales repeatedly asked the spirit who killed him before screaming and being killed in the dark.

events.action: Deducing the motive for the murder of Wales
events.description: Delzante receives word that the police matron has arrived and deduces that Wales was killed specifically to prevent the spirit's answer from identifying Spencer Lee's murderer.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame La Grange
events.action: Announcing upcoming physical searches
events.description: Delzante announces that a police matron will search the women while officer Grimshaw searches the men. He asks Madame La Grange to stay behind for further questioning before being searched.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame La Grange
events.action: Questioning Madame La Grange about the pre-arranged seance
events.description: Delzante asks Madame La Grange why she failed to deliver the pre-agreed answer when Wales asked for the killer's name. She claims she was in a trance and heard nothing.

events.action: Exposing the fake seance arrangement
events.description: Delzante produces written notes showing that Wales and Madame La Grange had rehearsed the seance script in advance. He explains Wales believed a woman killed Spencer Lee and wanted to trick her into confessing.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame La Grange
events.action: Demanding why the name was suppressed
events.description: Delzante reads aloud the script transcript up to where Madame La Grange was supposed to speak a woman's first name. He demands to know why she refused to utter the name, while she claims Wales never gave her a name.

events.action: Deducing an unexpected change of plans
events.description: Delzante asserts that something unexpected happened upon Madame La Grange's arrival that forced her to abandon the pre-arranged plan to name the female suspect.

events.action: Gathering the first names of female guests
events.description: Delzante systematically asks each woman in the room for her first name, taking note of Mary, Grace, Alice, and Helen.

events.action: Discovering a second woman named Helen
events.description: Miss O'Neill reveals her name is Helen, prompting Delzante to realize there are two women named Helen present in the room.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame La Grange
events.action: Accusing Madame La Grange of protecting Helen O'Neill
events.description: Delzante points out that Miss O'Neill was not present when La Grange arrived, making her an extra Helen. He accuses La Grange of altering seating arrangements and lying to protect Miss O'Neill.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante, Dick Crosby, and Madame La Grange
events.action: Provoking an emotional reaction
events.description: As Delzante continues pressing the accusation, Dick Crosby attempts to intervene to defend Helen O'Neill. Madame La Grange reacts emotionally, screaming at Delzante to leave the girl alone.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame La Grange
events.action: Formally accusing Helen O'Neill and ordering a search
events.description: Delzante explains that Helen sat next to Wales and could easily have freed one hand to stab him. Ignoring La Grange's frantic pleas, he orders the matron to search Helen for the murder weapon.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and Inspector Delzante
events.action: Revealing Helen is her daughter
events.description: To prevent the search, Madame La Grange admits that Helen O'Neill is her biological child and that seeing her unexpectedly made her panic and attempt to protect her.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and Helen O'Neill
events.action: Embracing and declaring innocence
events.description: Helen embraces Madame La Grange while La Grange vehemently insists to Inspector Delzante that her daughter is innocent and that she will prove it.

events.actor: Madame La Grange and Inspector Delzante
events.action: Pleading with the Inspector
events.description: Madame La Grange desperately begs Inspector Delzante to believe that Helen lacks a murderer's heart and vows to prove who the real killer is.

events.actor: Sir Roscoe Crosby and male guests
events.action: Protesting detention by police
events.description: As women are escorted to be searched, Sir Roscoe and other male guests vocally object to being detained and treated like common criminals.

events.action: Discussing waiting for instructions and searching for Madame Rosalie La Grange.
events.description: Richard explains to Lady Crosby that he does not know where Madame Rosalie La Grange has gone, noting that they were instructed to wait in the hall.

events.action: Praying alone in the dark room.
events.description: Left alone in the darkened room, Rosalie clasps her hands and prays aloud, admitting her past history as a fake medium while pleading for power to save her daughter.

events.action: Observing through the window and entering the room.
events.description: A police officer peers through the window blinds as Rosalie concludes her prayer. Inspector Delzante enters the room shortly after and questions why the lights were turned off.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and Madame Rosalie La Grange
events.action: Interrogating Rosalie in the room.
events.description: Delzante asks Rosalie why she turned off the lights and searched the room. She explains she was praying for guidance and seeking comfort regarding her daughter's innocence before Delzante orders her searched again.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante and police officer Ellis
events.action: Questioning the officer about window activity.
events.description: Inspector Delzante asks officer Ellis if anything was thrown out the window. Ellis confirms a woman lowered the blinds but threw nothing out, prompting Delzante to focus on Nellie.

events.actor: Inspector Delzante, Madame Rosalie La Grange, and Nellie O'Neill
events.action: Tricking Nellie into admitting presence in Spencer Lee's room.
events.description: Delzante lies that fingerprints on a cup match Nellie's, and when Nellie instinctively denies touching the cup, Delzante reveals there were no fingerprints and treats her denial as an admission of being present.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange, Nellie O'Neill, and Richard
events.action: Questioning Nellie about who she is protecting.
events.description: Rosalie and Richard plead with Nellie to explain her presence in Lee's room. Rosalie senses Nellie is lying to shield someone and demands to know who committed the crime.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange and Inspector Delzante
events.action: Bringing up the second Helen.
events.description: Rosalie tells Delzante that there were two Helens and urges him to question the other Helen. Delzante then directly questions Helen about her relationship with Spencer Lee.

events.action: Explaining the trip to retrieve letters.
events.description: Nellie states that Helen sent her to retrieve letters written to Spencer Lee before Helen's marriage to avoid blackmail. Delzante asks if tea was served before or after the letters were handed over.

events.action: Dismissing Nellie's account as a lie.
events.description: Delzante refuses to believe Nellie's story, asserting that she went for her own compromising letters and killed Spencer Lee when he refused to return them. Richard vigorously disputes Delzante's conclusion.

events.action: Denying writing letters to Spencer Lee.
events.description: Delzante asks Helen if she wrote letters to Lee or sent Nellie to retrieve them. Helen denies ever writing letters to Lee or requesting Nellie to visit his apartment.

events.action: Accusing Helen of lying to protect herself.
events.description: Richard accuses Helen of lying to save herself from suspicion, but Helen reiterates her statement. Delzante orders Officer Grimshaw to take Nellie into custody for police headquarters.

events.actor: Madame Rosalie La Grange and Inspector Delzante
events.action: Requesting ten minutes to solve the murder.
events.description: Rosalie begs Delzante not to arrest Nellie, claiming she knows who killed Spencer Lee. Delzante grants Rosalie ten minutes to reveal the killer and agrees to remove everyone else from the room.

events.action: paces alone in the room and laments her past trickery
events.description: Madame La Grange stands alone in the room, lamenting that all her life she relied on fake spiritualist tricks. She worries that she does not truly know who committed the crime to save her daughter.

events.action: implores her spirit guide 'Laughing Eyes' for help
events.description: Madame La Grange addresses her spirit guide, begging for a real message so she will not be defeated by a ruthless killer. She wrings her hands in distress as she prays.

events.action: enters the room after knocking
events.description: Inspector Delzante opens the door and walks into the room. Madame La Grange immediately asks to speak with him alone.

events.action: pleads with Inspector Delzante to try another seance
events.description: Madame La Grange begs Inspector Delzante to give her one more chance to stage a seance and trap the real murderer. She says she is drowning and snatching at a last straw.

events.action: grants Madame La Grange permission and orders Grimshaw to assist
events.description: Inspector Delzante agrees to her request despite calling it unheard of insanity. He orders Officer Grimshaw to follow Madame La Grange's instructions.

events.action: summons the protesting guests back into the seance room
events.description: Inspector Delzante informs the assembled guests in the hallway that they must return to the room. The guests express annoyance at the ongoing investigation.

events.action: re-enter the room and take their original seats
events.description: The guests slowly walk back into the seance room and prepare to sit down as instructed. Madame La Grange tells them to take their exact former positions.

events.action: protest against holding another seance near the deceased
events.description: Several guests shout in objection about sitting in the dark near the dead body. Madame La Grange counters that the innocent have no reason to fear the dead.

events.action: instructs everyone to hold hands and turns off the lights
events.description: Everyone sits in a circle and joins hands. Madame La Grange requests that the lights be extinguished to begin the spirit circle.

events.action: summons the spirit of Edward Wales in complete darkness
events.description: In pitch darkness, Madame La Grange chants repeatedly, calling upon the spirit of Edward Wales to reveal who killed him.

events.action: speaks in the darkness claiming to be Edward Wales
events.description: A deep voice echoes in the room, claiming to come from far away. The participants react with fear in the dark.

events.action: panics in the darkness and screams that someone pulled their hand away
events.description: Miss Eastwood screams in terror that someone next to her is moving and pulling their hand free in the dark circle.

events.action: screams hysterically and confesses to the murders
events.description: Miss Eastwood screams in terror that someone is touching her hair and striking her, hysterically yelling out that she did it.

events.action: turns on the lights as Miss Eastwood breaks down weeping
events.description: When the lights turn back on, Miss Eastwood is seen sobbing uncontrollably on her chair. Inspector Delzante commands Grimshaw to record her full confession.

events.action: confesses to killing both Wales and Spencer Lee
events.description: Inspector Delzante states that Miss Eastwood killed Wales to prevent him from receiving Lee's message, and killed Spencer Lee earlier. Miss Eastwood sobbing admits that she had to do it.

events.action: Crying out emotionally while seated in front of a standing man.
events.description: The woman in the black evening gown exclaims with emotional distress that the victim deserved what happened to him.

events.action: Speaking about her husband's departure and discovery of her affair.
events.description: She states that everyone thinks her husband went to London on business, but reveals he actually discovered her affair with Spencer and abandoned her.

events.actor: Inspector Donohue and Madame Rosalie La Grange
events.action: Standing near a door, listening attentively to the confession.
events.description: Inspector Donohue stands beside Madame Rosalie La Grange, listening closely as the confession unfolds across the room.

events.action: Recounting her hidden presence in Spencer's room.
events.description: She explains that she was hiding in Spencer's room on the day of the incident when another woman arrived.

events.action: Denouncing Spencer for his actions while she hid.
events.description: She tearfully accuses Spencer of being a beast for attempting to make love to the visitor while knowing she was hidden in the room.

events.action: Admitting to stabbing Spencer.
events.description: She confesses that after the other woman left, she lost control, grabbed a knife from his desk, and stabbed Spencer to death.

events.action: Pleading emotionally on her knees to stop further questioning.
events.description: Overwhelmed by distress, she sinks down while pleading frantically that enough has been revealed and begs to be spared further interrogation.

events.action: Inquiring about the empty chair and Richard's actions.
events.description: Inspector Donohue asks about Richard's location and notes that the chair was vacant when the lights were restored.

events.action: Explaining how the corpse's arm was rigged to point.
events.description: Madame Rosalie La Grange explains to Inspector Donohue that Mr. Richard placed a cane inside Mr. Wales's sleeve to prop his arm up in the air.

events.action: Excusing herself as Inspector Donohue turns to comfort his daughter.
events.description: Madame Rosalie La Grange steps aside politely as Inspector Donohue turns his attention toward comforting Nelly.

events.action: Walking out through the double doors toward the porch.
events.description: Madame Rosalie exits the main room through the doors, stepping onto the outdoor porch.

events.actor: Blonde young woman (Nelly) and Inspector Donohue
events.action: Admitting her previous lie regarding the letters while her father comforts her.
events.description: Nelly confesses off-screen to her father that she previously lied about Helen and the letters, and Inspector Donohue reassures her that he already knew.

events.action: Standing on the dark porch and addressing the spirits.
events.description: Standing alone outside on the porch, Madame Rosalie asks the unseen spirits whether the couple will live happily ever after, reminding them to rap once for yes and twice for no.

events.action: Gesturing on the porch as orchestral music closes the scene.
events.description: Madame Rosalie waits on the porch in the moonlight as dramatic orchestral music swells, bringing the story to a close.
